name: Alert Discord when a Trello card is overdue

nodes.name: Hourly Check
nodes.notes: Runs every hour. Cheap read, so frequent checking is fine; widen the interval if you prefer.

nodes.name: Get Cards on List
nodes.notes: Reads every card on the watched list. Retries 3x with backoff; failure exits the error output. Sample cards (one overdue, one future, one done-but-overdue) are pinned so you can test the Filter with no credential.

nodes.name: Compute Days Overdue
nodes.notes: Normalises each card and computes how many whole days past due it is (-1 when it has no due date).

nodes.name: Keep Overdue & Not Done
nodes.notes: Keeps only cards due in the past (daysOverdue >= 0) that are NOT marked complete. A tidy board yields zero items here, so nothing posts.

nodes.name: Format Overdue Alert
nodes.notes: Builds one alert per overdue card. Runs once per item that passed the Filter.

nodes.name: Post Alert to Discord
nodes.notes: Posts one Discord alert per overdue card via webhook. Retries 3x with backoff.

nodes.name: Capture Failure Context
nodes.notes: Error rail: records why the check failed.

nodes.name: Alert: Check Failed
nodes.notes: Error rail: surfaces a broken check so overdue work doesn't go unwatched.

# Alert Discord when a Trello card is overdue

**Pattern:** Schedule -> read -> filter -> alert · **Level:** Production · **Trigger:** Schedule (hourly)

## What it does
Reads a Trello list on a timer and posts a Discord alert for each card that is past its due date and not marked complete. Silent when nothing is overdue.

## Why it exists
Due dates only help if someone notices they've passed. This watches the list for you and nudges — per card — the moment work slips, without a human chasing the board.

## Main flow
Hourly Check -> Get Cards on List -> Compute Days Overdue -> Keep Overdue & Not Done -> Format Alert -> Post to Discord (failure -> error rail).

## Use it for
- Chasing card owners when a deadline slips
- An SLA-style watch on an ops/support list
- Keeping a deadline-driven board honest hands-off

## You get
- Per-card overdue nudges, automatically
- No message at all when the board is clean
- Alerts that link straight to the card

## Before first run
Connect credentials: Trello API; Discord webhook URL.
Colour key: 🟦 entry · 🟫 app I/O · ⬜ logic · 🟩 output · 🟥 error rail.
Each node has its own doc card underneath — read those before editing.

## Try it now
This runs on a timer; the Trello read is pinned (with one overdue, one future, one done card) so you can test the Filter with no credential. Sample data is pinned on the trigger, so hit **Execute Workflow** to watch it flow end to end before attaching a single credential. Right-click → Unpin when you go live.

## Credentials setup

Credentials are never bundled in a template. Every node that talks to an external service needs its own connection before the first real run — open the node, click the Credential dropdown, choose **Create new**.

**Trello API**
Trello → click your avatar → Power-Ups admin → API key; then authorize a token from the same page. n8n's Trello credential takes the API key + token.
_Gotcha:_ The token must belong to an account that is a member of the board, or every call 401s.

**Discord webhook URL**
Server Settings → Integrations → Webhooks → New Webhook → Copy Webhook URL. Paste it into n8n's Discord Webhook credential.
_Gotcha:_ A webhook URL is bound to one channel. Use a separate webhook/credential per channel you post to.

Set each credential up once; it is reusable across every workflow in your instance.

## Troubleshooting

**Nothing happens when the event should fire**
Cause: The workflow is still a draft, or its trigger is inactive.
Fix: Publish/activate it. The manual test URL is different from the production URL.

**A node shows a red triangle right after import**
Cause: No credential is attached yet.
Fix: Expected on a fresh import — open the node and attach a credential (see the Credentials note).

**Done cards still get alerts**
Cause: dueComplete isn't being read, or you use a label instead of the due-complete checkbox.
Fix: This keys off Trello's due-complete flag. If you track 'done' with a label, add that label to the Filter.

**No alerts even though cards look overdue**
Cause: The dates are timezone-shifted, or the cards have no due date set.
Fix: daysOverdue is -1 when a card has no due date. Confirm the cards actually carry a due date.

**Provider returns 429**
Cause: You are hitting the API rate limit.
Fix: The node already retries with backoff; widen the schedule interval or lower the batch size to stay under quota.

Still stuck? The **Executions** tab shows the exact node that failed and the data going into it — start there.

## Design decisions

There is no Loop node: the Discord node naturally executes once per item, so the Filter's output *is* the fan-out. 'Days overdue' is computed once in a Set node so the Filter and the message share the same number. Keeping the check silent on a clean board is deliberate — an alert channel that only speaks when something is wrong is one people keep un-muted.

## Practice exercises

Already production-shaped — deepen it:

1. Escalate cards over 3 days overdue by @mentioning a role.
2. Group all overdue cards into a single digest instead of one message each.
3. Read several lists and tag each alert with its list name.

## 🛠 Customize me

Tune the hourly cadence and the watched list (`TRELLO_LIST_ID`). The overdue rule lives in **Compute Days Overdue** + **Keep Overdue & Not Done** — change `daysOverdue >= 0` to add a grace period. To escalate, add a second Filter branch for `daysOverdue > 3` that @mentions a role.

## 🔐 Security

Read-only Trello token. Only card names and due dates leave to Discord. If you track 'done' with a label instead of the due-complete checkbox, add that label to the filter so finished work isn't flagged as overdue.
